title: An injury-related dismissal can produce a reinstatement and lost-pay order while actual compliance remains unverified
source_unit: Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 2621 concerning Alam Shah
geography: Greenacre, Sydney, Australia; Fair Work Commission case [2025] FWC 2621

observations.period: April 17-September 5, 2025; workplace injury, return, dismissal, tribunal review, and remedy order

injury_and_return.value: Mr Shah was struck by a forklift on April 17, took time off on workers compensation, and returned to work on April 28, 2025

dismissal_and_access.value: He was dismissed by email on May 2 without a valid reason or opportunity to respond; the case records limited English, interpreter use, and a local walkable job that was difficult to replace because he did not drive

remedy_order.value: The Commission ordered reinstatement to the former position within 14 days, continuity of service, translation/publication in Rohingya, and $18,035.56 for 20 weeks of lost pay less one week in lieu of notice

receipt_and_durability.unit: missing post-order payment receipt, actual return, work duration, recurrence, household recovery, trust, collective action, and exit

mechanism.value: A tribunal can convert an injury-related dismissal and language-access dispute into a reinstatement and lost-pay order while leaving the affected worker's preferred remedy, actual compliance, and durable livelihood unresolved

observations.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision and translated publication route; injury, return, dismissal, language/cultural access, remedy preference, order, and open compliance are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The decision reports the injury, dismissal, context, and order but no post-order receipt or follow-up. Private medical, payroll, household, alternative-job, compliance, and later-employment records are not retained.
observations.subgroup: One publicly identified worker in an Australian employment-remedy case; no population denominator or comparison group is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: The employer may have had workplace concerns not sustained by the evidence, and a formal reinstatement order may not match the worker's preferred compensation remedy; an order is not verified restoration.

boundary: This record establishes one adjudicated worker case with observed injury, return, dismissal, language/cultural access, tribunal response, reinstatement, continuity, and lost-pay order. It does not establish post-order compliance, payment receipt, restored livelihood, trust, recurrence, collective action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the public FWC decision; private worker, payroll, medical, household, and compliance files are not retained.
